data.one_liner: LiteRT-LM on-device engine for flutter_edge_ai supporting .litertlm models and embeddings.
data.what_it_does: Provides a LiteRT-LM engine implementation for the flutter_edge_ai package, running .litertlm models, EmbeddingGemma 2 embeddings, and LiteRT .tflite embeddings across multiple native platforms and web via FFI. It handles sessions, streaming, structured outputs, and platform-specific execution on CPU, GPU, and NPU.
use_when: You are using flutter_edge_ai and need to run .litertlm language models or embeddings on-device.
You want support for structured outputs (JSON schema) via LiteRT-LM constrained decoding.
You need multi-platform on-device inference across Android, iOS, web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
avoid_when: You are not using flutter_edge_ai in your application.
Your application relies strictly on cloud-based LLM APIs and does not require local on-device inference.
strengths: Runs models locally across various hardware targets including CPU, GPU, and NPU.
Supports structured output via JSON schema validation.
Integrated deeply with the flutter_edge_ai ecosystem and model catalog.
weaknesses: Requires strict version matching and upgrading of multiple dependent flutter_edge_ai packages together.
NPU and certain platforms have specific limitations regarding session sharing, samplers, or context windows.
data.setup_notes: Requires pairing with flutter_edge_ai, registering the LiteRtLmEngine during initialization, and adhering to strict package version requirements alongside other edge AI packages.

alternatives.name: tflite_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want direct TensorFlow Lite model execution without the specific flutter_edge_ai framework abstraction.

alternatives.name: llamadart
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer running LLaMA models via llama.cpp bindings rather than LiteRT-LM.

alternatives.name: firebase_ai
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want to use cloud-backed AI models instead of local on-device execution.
